The Causal Graph Builder (NOTEARs) operates as an inverse covariance selection method, imposing sparsity through L1 regularization on the precision matrix. This enforces acyclicity constraints, enabling discovery of directed relationships among observable variables. Hierarchical Live Probit models skill evolution via Gaussian random walks, providing dynamic win probabilities while accounting for team-specific heterogeneity. Dynamic Probit Variational Bayes scales this framework to high-dimensional covariate spaces using stochastic optimization, making it suitable for real-time betting applications. Copula Hidden Markov Models capture non-linear temporal dependencies and tail asymmetries in multi-variate outcomes, offering robust risk assessment for portfolio construction. These four primitives form a coherent epistemological chain: causal discovery → dynamic probabilistic modeling → approximate inference → uncertainty quantification. Their dual nature—operating both as standalone tools and components within larger systems—demands careful consideration of telemetry metrics such as edge recovery rates, ELBO convergence, and predictive coverage. Failure occurs when structural assumptions (acyclicity, Gaussianity, mean-field) are violated by complex, non-stationary data generating processes.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The NOTEARs algorithm generalizes the graphical lasso (Friedman et al., 2008) to directed graphs, drawing from information geometry and exponential families. The hierarchical probit model extends the classical Bradley-Terry framework (Bradley & Terry, 1952) into a mixed-effects paradigm. Stochastic variational inference (Hoffman et al., 2013) provides scalable approximate Bayes, while copula-based time series (Joe, 2014) offer flexible multivariate dependence modeling beyond linear correlation.
